CopyCustomUtils.doc: Copy a file or folder you specify between the quotes to each instance folder, if the file/folder is located in Nucleus folder\utils\User. This function also accepts two additional parameters, a relative path from the game root folder if the file needs to be placed somewhere else within instance folder and one parameter to indicate which instances to copy the file to if it only needs to be in some. Use of parameters is separated by a | character. So it would look something like this [ "filename.ini|\\bin|1,2" ]. RegisterRawInputHook.doc: This hook will unsubscribe the game from Raw Input (if it has already subscribed to it), and then subscribes Proto Input to receive raw input instead. Raw input received is forwarded back to the game if it uses raw input. Proto Input receives all keyboard/mouse input from this hook so it always needs to be enabled.
RegisterRawInputHook.practice: This is the switch that makes Proto Input read each player's own keyboard and mouse: installing it is the only place Proto Input registers its raw input window, and it takes raw input away from the game (the game's own registrations are redirected to Proto Input). Everything per-player for keyboards and mice depends on it: the Send…Messages options post each player's input to their window, and the cursor and key state hooks (GetCursorPosHook, GetKeyStateHook, …) answer from the state it fills. Without it those hooks see no keys pressed and a frozen cursor. 503 of the 567 Hub handlers that use Proto Input turn it on, 229 of them from Game.ProtoInput.OnInputLocked with ProtoInput.InstallHook.

GetRawInputDataHook.doc: When forwarding the input back to the game, you need to create a handle to the input data. However these handles can only be created by Windows. To get around this, Proto Input will send a dummy WM_INPUT message to the game (from the Register Raw Input hook). The game then calls GetRawInputData using the dummy handle. This hook intercepts the call and passes in the saved data. This hook is required to make forwarding raw input work, so it should always be enabled.
GetRawInputDataHook.practice: Only matters for games that read raw input themselves. With Game.ProtoInput.RegisterRawInputHook on, Proto Input posts each player's raw input as WM_INPUT to the windows the game registered, tagged with its own signature; this hook lets the game's GetRawInputData read that data. Without the raw input hook it has nothing to pass on. 500 of the 567 Hub handlers that use Proto Input turn it on, nearly all together with the raw input hook (497).

DinputDeviceHook.doc:
